importance_ranking.reason: Log cabins are high-value, aesthetically-driven structures where buyers — resort developers, eco-tourism operators, homeowners — make initial shortlisting decisions based on visual style, finish quality, and structural form. Extreme visual variation exists across sub-types (A-frame, gable-roof resort cabin, rooftop cabin, garden cabin), making image the primary scan-and-filter signal before any text is read.

Built type (prefab vs on-site), wood species, floor area, and treatment are non-interchangeable parameters that define project feasibility, cost, and compliance — buyers cannot shortlist without confirming these match their project requirement.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: No nationally recognised brand commands buyer recall in the Indian log cabin market — buyers search by spec, style, and service capability rather than manufacturer name; Deodar Group and Royal Prefab are known within the trade but are not consumer-facing brands buyers search for by name.
importance_ranking.reason: End-to-end service capability (design, fabrication, installation, after-sales) and track record of completed resort/residential projects are critical vendor selection criteria for high-value custom structures; institutional buyers (state tourism boards, forest departments) additionally require company credentials and prior project references.

Price varies substantially with wood species, floor area, built type, and furnishing level — buyers discover and compare across spec tiers during search, making price a spec-dependent qualifier rather than a standalone commodity comparison signal. Indian buyers are price-sensitive but cannot compare prices without spec equivalence first.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Standard portable/catalogue cabins (fixed sizes such as 10×10 ft, 10×20 ft) may be quoted per piece — unit must be shown to prevent misreading of price when sellers mix per-sq-ft and per-piece quoting conventions.
importance_ranking.reason: Per sq ft is the dominant quoting unit for custom-dimensioned log cabins, but some sellers quote per piece for standard portable units — without the unit shown, buyers cannot compare prices across listings or interpret quoted figures accurately.

top_configurator_specs.reason: Prefab, on-site build, and knock-down are non-interchangeable construction methods that drive fundamentally different project timelines, logistics costs, and total price — a buyer cannot substitute one for another based on their site, budget, or permit situation.

Wood species (pine, spruce, cedar, teak, engineered wood) determines structural durability, climate suitability, treatment requirements, and a significant price delta — cedar commands a premium over SPF pine and is non-interchangeable for humid or coastal deployments.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Log wall thickness (e.g. 70mm, 90mm, 120mm) is a primary structural and insulation differentiator that drives material cost and thermal performance — buyers in hill-station and cold-climate deployments specify minimum thickness as a project requirement.

Whether the price includes on-site installation and erection is a critical scope-of-supply question for buyers comparing sellers — some quote supply-only while others quote supply-and-install, making this a primary price comparability gate.

top_rfq_specs.reason: Intended use (resort/hotel, farmhouse, personal retreat, backyard office, guard cabin) routes the RFQ to sellers with the right product range, scale capability, and compliance experience — a resort developer and a backyard-office buyer require fundamentally different structures and sellers.

Floor area is the primary scope and pricing variable for custom log cabins — sellers need this to determine whether the project falls within their fabrication capacity and to provide an accurate per-sq-ft quotation.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Whether the buyer needs a prefabricated modular unit, an on-site handcrafted build, or a knock-down relocatable cabin determines which sellers can respond — not all suppliers offer all construction methods.

buyer_spec_audit.image_upload_reason: Log cabin design varies extensively within the same spec combination — the same wood type, area, and intended use can describe dozens of visually distinct structures (A-frame, gable-roof chalet, flat-roof garden cabin, multi-room resort cottage). Resort developers and hospitality buyers typically have a specific architectural style or reference project in mind; an uploaded image or design reference allows sellers to confirm they can match the aesthetic and structural form, avoiding misaligned quotations.
